`nvs pkg fetch` materialises the graph under `vendor/` and writes **one generated Novis source file**,
`vendor/packages.nvs`, containing nothing but ordinary declarations:

```nvs
<?nvs
// Generated by `nvs pkg` from package.lock. Do not edit.
autoload 'Acme\Csv' from './acme/csv/src';
autoload 'Acme\Http' from './acme/http/src';
```

The application `require`s that file once. **That is the entire integration.** Name resolution is
exactly `rule:programs/autoload`'s — paths written as string literals, relative to the declaring file, no runtime loader
(`rule:programs/no-runtime-autoload`), no walk-up search, no new invalidation edge — and the compiler
learns nothing about packages in order to resolve a name. The proof is structural: `nvs-syntax` and
`nvs-types` gain no package-aware code path for name resolution at all.

**The generated file is committed.** It is short and readable, and every change to the dependency
graph shows up in a diff as a line of source rather than as a change in a tool's behaviour.

The prefix each line names is the package's name (`rule:packaging/a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name`).
Each package is written to `vendor/<vendor>/<name>/`, its slug as a path, so the folder of a package
does not move when its version does. Beside each `autoload` line, the fetch writes one grant line for
the same package into `[grants]`, an empty one included
(`rule:security/an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application`), and never rewrites a grant line a
person already edited (`rule:packaging/package-toml-is-a-tool-input`). The line is the subtree form,
`'Acme\Http\*' = []`, because a package's code is its namespace and every namespace below it, and a
package that already has a key naming its namespace, in either form, gets no line.

**Not on disk.** `nvs pkg fetch` and `nvs pkg vendor` write the folders, the generated file and the
grant lines (`crates/nvs-cli/src/package/fetch.rs`). `nvs pkg add` and `nvs pkg update` write them through the same code
(`crates/nvs-cli/src/package/minimum.rs`).
